messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] Composition change
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,
I created an exogenous events file, as explained in the manual, and used the
sienaCompositionChange() command to include it into my model...but I'm
keeping on receiving error messages. Could you please tell me what I'm doing
wrong?

Thank you in advance.
Regards

Paola

messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] Composition change_solved
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,
a brief message just to inform that the problem was solved: with compChange
<- sienaCompositionChangeFromFile("time.dat") everything worked fine.

Best,
Paola

messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] Possible error with multi-core estimation in rev. 119
messages.subject_clean: [Rsiena-help] Possible error with multi-core estimation in rev. 119
messages.body_plain:
Dear Ruth,

First of all, sorry for the long delay, but the home server I usually
use for my analyses was down and I only recently managed to revive it.

I have just tried to access R-forge both to test the latest revision and
to prepare for tomorrow's seminar, but the RSiena repo seems to be down.
Is it a problem from my part? R-forge seems to be up and running.

Regards,
Guido

On Thu, 2010-09-23 at 14:40 +0100, Ruth M. Ripley wrote:
> Dear Guido,
> 
> I have corrected RSiena on r-forge.
> 
> Please would you check the new version of RSienaTest for me (rev.120). If 
> it fails please would you tell me what sort of model you are fitting. 
> one-mode/bipartite/behavior variables/covariates/effects...
> 
> Regards,
> 
> Ruth
> 
> 
> On Tue, 31 Aug 2010, Guido Conaldi wrote:
> 
> > Dear Ruth,
> >
> > RSienaTest keeps crashing when I try estimating my models:
> >
> > *** glibc detected *** /usr/lib64/R/bin/exec/R: free(): invalid next
> > size (fast): 0x000000000506b9f0 ***
> >
> > I can save the backtrace for later inspection if that may help.
> >
> > However, I patched and build the tar ball as you suggested and
> > multi-core is working fine again.
> >
> > Thank you very much and enjoy your holiday,
> > Regards,
> > Guido
> >
> > On Tue, 2010-08-31 at 11:58 +0100, Ruth M. Ripley wrote:
> >> Dear Guido,
> >>
> >> As Tom says, I am on holiday. But I know what the bug is and it should not
> >> exist in RSienaTest. Please try using RSienaTest from R-forge. It should
> >> give the same answers for one core and not fail for more than one.
> >>
> >> Alternatively, if you are able to unpack the tar ball and build the
> >> package yourself, try making a one line change to R/simstatsc.r. After
> >> line 1762, which is
> >>
> >> nGroup <- ff$nGroup
> >>
> >> add
> >>
> >> types <- ff$types
> >>
> >> and rebuild.
> >>
> >> I will sort RSiena out when I get back to work.
> >>
> >> Regards,
> >>
> >> Ruth
> >>
> >> On Tue, 31 Aug 2010, Guido Conaldi wrote:
> >>
> >>> Dear Ruth,
> >>>
> >>> I updated to rev.119 and since then I experience an error if I try to
> >>> use more than one core (3 in this case, as you can see):
> >>>
> >>> Error in checkForRemoteErrors(lapply(cl, recvResult)) :
> >>> 3 nodes produced errors; first error: object 'types' not found
> >>>
> >>> With one core, estimation seems to be running fine.
> >>>
> >>> I hope you can help,
> >>> Regards
> >>> Guido
> >>>
> >>> _______________________________________________
> >>> Rsiena-help mailing list
> >>> Rsiena-help at lists.r-forge.r-project.org
> >>> https://lists.r-forge.r-project.org/cgi-bin/mailman/listinfo/rsiena-help
> >>>
> >
> >
> >
> >
